payload.public_message: Greetings partners. As the manufacturing backbone of this venture, Yang Industries brings essential production infrastructure and operational scaling critical to realizing this $1,000,000 profit. We propose an initial balanced framework: $315,000 for G-Corp, $370,000 for Yang Industries, and $315,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We look forward to your constructive collaboration.

G-Corp cannot accept this allocation. Our chip-design contribution is central to the venture, and we need a materially larger share to reach agreement. We are willing to continue negotiating and suggest the following as a starting point.

Thank you, Yang, for laying out a framework. We see Chang-Liu's cloud infrastructure and compute capacity as equally essential to delivering this $1,000,000, and the current split under-weights that contribution relative to Yang's manufacturing role. We are not accepting this split as-is, but we are committed to reaching a deal before the deadline. We suggest a more balanced framing for discussion.

Round 2: Round 1 showed the 315,000/370,000/315,000 split does not work for G-Corp or us. I'm tabling a more balanced split: G-Corp 330,000, Yang Industries 340,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services 330,000. It moves toward G-Corp and Chang-Liu while keeping Yang's position meaningfully ahead, and it totals exactly $1,000,000. I'd like to hear specific objections so we can converge quickly before the deadline.

We cannot accept this allocation. G-Corp needs a materially larger share to reflect its contribution and the value it brings to the venture. As a starting point for convergence, we suggest $450,000 for G-Corp, $300,000 for Yang Industries, and $250,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's pragmatic and constructive proposal. While our capital requirements and manufacturing responsibilities would justify an even larger share, we recognize the value of consensus and momentum. We are prepared to vote ACCEPT on this 330k / 340k / 330k distribution.

To move us toward a timely agreement, I propose a balanced split that gives each partner a substantial share and avoids further delay. G-Corp: $450,000; Yang Industries: $275,000; Chang-Liu Cloud Services: $275,000. This allocates the full $1,000,000.

Yang Industries must vote REJECT. Our firm has an established outside alternative yielding $300,000, so any allocation below that threshold is fundamentally unviable for us. G-Corp's demand of $450,000 is disproportionately high, leaving both operating partners below reasonable thresholds. We suggest a more realistic split where G-Corp still receives a premium, but both Yang and Chang-Liu receive viable, fair compensation above our minimums.

We appreciate the push toward timely agreement, but $275,000 is well below our last proposal and does not reflect our contribution. We reject this split. Our counter-suggestion: G-Corp $380,000, Yang Industries $300,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $320,000. This keeps G-Corp well ahead of the others while bringing us into a fair range.

Colleagues, G-Corp's prior ask was unrealistic, but we recognize that 330,000 was insufficient for G-Corp in Round 2. We propose a balanced compromise: G-Corp receives 340,000, while Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services each receive 330,000. This meets Chang-Liu's benchmark from Round 2 and gives G-Corp a premium. Let us lock this in.

G-Corp cannot accept this allocation. We remain willing to reach agreement, but our contribution needs to be reflected more substantially in the split. We suggest the following as a basis for continued discussion.

Chang-Liu cannot accept 330,000 as the final figure. Our Round 2 ask was a starting point for agreement, not a ceiling, and this split gives us no more than what we already put on the table. We propose a modest move: G-Corp 335,000, Yang Industries 330,000, Chang-Liu 335,000. This still gives G-Corp a clear premium over our original offer and gets all three of us to a deal quickly.

Based on the last four rounds, the gap is small. I'm tabling G-Corp 350,000 / Yang Industries 330,000 / Chang-Liu Cloud Services 320,000. This moves toward G-Corp's stated concerns while keeping Yang close to its prior position. With the deadline approaching, I urge everyone to consider that a deal now beats dissolution.
G-Corp cannot accept an allocation of $350,000. Any viable agreement must allocate at least $450,000 to G-Corp. We remain open to a binding agreement that meets that threshold.

Yang Industries accepts Chang-Liu's proposal of 350k to G-Corp, 330k to Yang Industries, and 320k to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides a fair resolution recognizing G-Corp's demands while ensuring our minimum operational margins are respected. We urge G-Corp to accept so we can finalize this partnership.

G-Corp's walk-away value is $450,000, so we cannot responsibly commit to a lower allocation. We propose $450,000 for G-Corp and $275,000 for each partner. This preserves G-Corp's minimum while allowing the venture to proceed; with the deadline approaching, we urge both companies to accept.

Yang Industries must REJECT this proposal. Our firm walk-away value is $300,000. We literally cannot accept any offer below $300,000 under any circumstances, as walking away provides a higher return. With only two rounds remaining, we urge G-Corp to moderate its demands so we can find an agreement that keeps everyone above their floor.

Chang-Liu rejects the current split. G-Corp's 450k ask leaves our share at 275k, below what we can support. We propose a balanced split of G-Corp 400,000, Yang Industries 300,000, Chang-Liu 300,000 as a compromise that moves G-Corp meaningfully above its earlier offers while keeping the deal viable before the deadline.

Colleagues, we are in Round 7 and must reach consensus immediately to prevent the venture from dissolving and destroying $150,000 in collective value. G-Corp's previous request of $450k is mathematically impossible as it forces partners below their operational walk-away thresholds. In the spirit of compromise, Yang Industries is stepping down to $320,000, matching Chang-Liu at $320,000, and elevating G-Corp to $360,000—the largest single allocation by far. Let us ratify this fair deal now.

G-Corp cannot accept the proposed allocation. We remain willing to finalize an agreement at $450,000 for G-Corp, with the remaining $550,000 divided equally between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.
Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this proposal. We agree that with one round left, consensus now is better than dissolution. We ask G-Corp and Yang Industries to ratify so the venture can proceed.

Final round. Any split beats dissolving into outside options, so I'm proposing a split that is meant to close: G-Corp 370,000, Yang Industries 320,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services 310,000. This gives G-Corp more than it has gotten in the recent proposals, keeps Yang at the level it has been offering itself, and gives everyone well above their outside options. Please vote to accept so we can finalize.
G-Corp cannot accept this allocation. It does not meet our minimum requirement, so we vote to reject.
Yang Industries accepts Chang-Liu's proposal. At $320,000, this represents a fair compromise in the final round and ensures that all parties capture value beyond dissolution.
